title: Choosing without the lineup
question: How do binomial coefficients count the ways to choose k items from n?
hook: Picking a starting team ignores who stands where, and that one fact explains every entry in Pascal's triangle.
idea: A binomial coefficient counts the unordered choices of k items from n.

beats.prompt: You try to choose 5 elements from a set that has only 3. How many ways are there?

choices.label: One way: take all three elements
choices.feedback: Taking all three is not choosing five, so it does not count.

choices.label: Zero ways, since entries past the edge are zero
Ten ways, the same as 5 choose 3
choices.feedback: Choosing five from only three is not the same question as choosing three from five.

beats.explain: Entries of Pascal's triangle past its edges are all zero, and terms with k > n are zero.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it counts or means
pairs: the number of ways to choose k out of n objects
the number of k-permutations of n
sequences of k distinct objects, order kept
sequences that define the same k-combination
beats.explain: C counts choices, P counts ordered selections, and in the product formula the top counts ordered sequences while the bottom counts those that give the same group.

beats.prompt: Put the steps for building (n k) from the start of row n in order
items: Start at the leftmost coefficient of row n, which is 1
Compute the next coefficient to its right
Keep moving right, one coefficient at a time
Stop when you reach the k-th coefficient
beats.explain: Starting from the leftmost value of 1, each coefficient is worked out from the previous one until the k-th is reached.

beats.prompt: A coach picks 3 of 8 starters, order ignored. One step in this count is wrong; which?
steps: The coach picks 3 starters from 8 and order does not matter.
Each group of three is counted once in those ordered picks.
So the number of groups is 8 × 7 × 6.
beats.explain: One group shows up as several different ordered sequences, so the ordered count must be reduced by the denominator that counts those repeats.
